title: Sarah Mosseri, author of Trust Fall, reads the FedMart board against her own research — 'trust is not a thing a company has'
summary: Mosseri studies workplace equity and wrote Trust Fall, a book about how organisations hollow out the trust they advertise. Reading Incorruptible, she stops on a line about FedMart's board and recognises her own subject in it: a board treating the trust Sol Price had built with customers as latitude to spend rather than a relationship to maintain. She uses the case to sharpen her own argument — that trust is not an asset a company holds but a reflection of relationships requiring continued investment — and reads its fetishization as hollowing out how people connect at work.
blockquote: Organizations celebrate trust, measure it, put it in rankings, because trust buys latitude. What gets lost is that trust is not a thing a company has. Trust reflects relationships that must be maintained and invested in.
attribution_title: Workplace equity researcher · author, Trust Fall
